plain_explanation: Tokens are model-specific pieces of input, not always words. Attention combines representations using weights. A causal mask stops a decoder using future positions. Encoders suit understanding inputs; decoders generate continuations; encoder-decoder models read an input and generate a corresponding output.
worked_example: Weights 0.25, 0.65 and 0.10 sum to 1. A token in position two cannot see position three under a causal mask. Scores [1,2,-infinity] produce weights about [0.269,0.731,0]. A large attention weight alone does not establish causal explanation or factual accuracy.

exam.question: Why does a decoder use a causal mask?
exam.model_answer: To ensure generation at a position depends only on permitted earlier/current positions, not future target tokens.

exam.question: For weights 0.25, 0.65, 0.10, which input receives most weight?
exam.model_answer: The second input, with 0.65. The three weights sum to 1.

exam.question: Choose a model role for translating one sentence into another language.
exam.model_answer: An encoder-decoder design is a suitable example: read the source then generate the target. Other architectures can also translate.
